name: list_issue_observations
description: List observation-level evidence for one issue, cursor-paginated. Use search_issues to find the issueId, and get_observation for full detail on one observation.

cursor.description: Opaque continuation token returned as nextCursor by the prior response

name: search_applications
description:
Search applications by name, tag, or custom metadata. Returns every application when no
filters are given. This is the discovery tool for the appId parameter used by
application-scoped tools.

Example: name="petclinic", metadataFilters='{"team":"payments"}'

name.description: Text search filter (searches name, contextPath, tags, metadata)

metadataFilters.description: JSON object for metadata filters. Format: {"field":"value"} or {"field":["v1","v2"]}. Multiple fields use AND logic. Multiple values within a field use OR logic. Field names and values are case-insensitive. Values must be non-empty.

name: search_incidents
description:
Search incidents across the authenticated organization with optional filters.

Use search_applications first to find an application ID from an application name, then pass applicationIds.

Unlike search_attacks, this tool searches unified security incidents. Use search_issues with hasIncident=true to find the issues behind incidents.

For a count alone, call with no cursor and pageSize=1, then read totalItems.

Examples:
- Open critical production incidents: statuses="OPEN", severities="CRITICAL", deploymentTiers="PRODUCTION"
- Incidents for one application in a window: applicationIds="app-uuid", startTime="2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
- Attack-driven incidents by text: searchTerms="sql injection", dataTypes="ATTACK"

cursor.description: Opaque continuation token returned as nextCursor by the prior response. Send the same filters and sort as the first page. Omit for the first page.

sort.description: Sort as property,DIRECTION. Valid properties: assignedUserName, createdAt, incidentId, name, score, status, updatedAt. Use score to sort by risk because severity is derived from score. Valid directions: ASC, DESC. Default: createdAt,DESC

startTime.description: Filter by start timestamp. Accepts ISO-8601 timestamp with timezone, e.g. 2025-01-15T10:30:00Z, or epoch milliseconds. Date-only values are rejected. Default: no start-time lower bound.

endTime.description: Filter by end timestamp. Accepts ISO-8601 timestamp with timezone, e.g. 2025-01-16T10:30:00Z, or epoch milliseconds. Date-only values are rejected. Default: no end-time upper bound.

applicationIds.description: Comma-separated application IDs. Default: all applications.

statuses.description: Comma-separated statuses: OPEN,CLOSED. Default: all statuses

severities.description: Comma-separated severities: CRITICAL,HIGH,MEDIUM,LOW,NOTE. Default: all severities

assignedUserIds.description: Comma-separated assigned user IDs. Default: all assigned users

deploymentTiers.description: Comma-separated deployment tiers: DEVELOPMENT,QA,PRODUCTION. Default: all deployment tiers

searchTerms.description: Search terms. Default: no text search

dataTypes.description: Comma-separated data types: VULNERABILITY,ATTACK,BEHAVIOR. Default: all data types

targets.description: Comma-separated targets: CODE,LIBRARY. Default: all targets

sensors.description: Comma-separated sensors: CONTRAST_AGENT,CONTRAST_SMART_SCAN. Default: all sensors

techniques.description: Comma-separated techniques: RUNTIME,STATIC. Default: all techniques

name: list_issues_by_library
description:
List open issues linked to one library within an application's library tree. An issue matches when the requested library is the root library or a transitive library beneath it, so issue titles may name a related library rather than the queried one; do not post-filter results by title.

Use search_applications to find application IDs, then list_application_libraries to find library hashes.

name: search_cves
description:
Search CVEs across the authenticated NorthStar organization for CVE Shield exposure and risk.

Use list_applications_by_cve only for Classic/TeamServer CVE impact; this tool searches NorthStar CVE Shield data. Use search_applications first to find application IDs by name.

Shield fields reflect agent-reported activity as of each agent's last report; use get_cve_impact for configured policy.

highestShieldStatus is the largest activity ordinal in NO_SHIELD < SHIELD_OFF < NOT_SEEN < PROTECTING < EXPOSED < BLOCKED < EXPLOITED, not risk order; Insights counts CVEs by it.

Page 1 carries totalItems; for counts, use pageSize=1.

Examples:
- Highest-risk CVEs: sort="maxCvssScore,DESC"
- Shielded CVEs with exposure somewhere: cveShieldExists=true, shieldStatuses="EXPOSED,EXPLOITED"
- CVEs observed in production for selected applications: appIds="app-uuid", environments="PRODUCTION"

keyword.description: CVE ID prefix match. Suffix fragments like '44228' never match. Year-anchored fragments like '2021' or '2021-44228' get 'CVE-' prepended. Matches CVE IDs only, not library names. Default: no text search.

severities.description: Comma-separated severities: CRITICAL,HIGH,MEDIUM,LOW,NOTE. Severity derives from Contrast-adjusted CVSS (application criticality and shield protection lower it), so CRITICAL can exclude shielded CVEs. Default: all severities.

shieldStatuses.description: Comma-separated shield statuses: NO_SHIELD,SHIELD_OFF,NOT_SEEN,PROTECTING,EXPOSED,BLOCKED,EXPLOITED. NO_SHIELD: no shield applies (none configured, non-Java stack, or agent below the minimum version). SHIELD_OFF: shield configured with mode OFF. NOT_SEEN: shield in MONITOR or BLOCK mode with no traffic yet. The rest are observed traffic results. Matches when any observed environment has a selected status; null environments never match. Combined with environments, EXPOSED plus PRODUCTION means observed in production and exposed somewhere, not exposed in production.

cveShieldExists.description: Filter by whether agents have reported CVE Shield activity for the CVE. Default: either state.

appIds.description: Comma-separated application IDs. Results cover only applications visible to the caller. Inaccessible IDs in a mixed list are silently dropped; if every ID is inaccessible the request returns a permissions error. Default: all visible applications.

environments.description: Comma-separated observed deployment tiers: DEVELOPMENT,QA,PRODUCTION. Independent of shieldStatuses. Default: all tiers.

sort.description: Sort as property,DIRECTION. Valid properties: cveId,cveShieldExists,maxCvssScore,noShieldCount,shieldOffCount,notSeenCount,protectingCount,exposedCount,blockedCount,exploitedCount,numApplications,numEnvironments,numLibraryVersions. EPSS is not sortable. Valid directions: ASC,DESC. Default: maxCvssScore,DESC. A cveId tie-breaker is appended.

cursor.description: Opaque continuation token returned as nextCursor by the prior response.

name: search_vulnerabilities
description:
Search vulnerabilities detected by Contrast Assess across all applications in the
organization.

Use search_app_vulnerabilities instead when scoping to one application or filtering by
session metadata or latest session.

A result's environments field reflects only its latest instance and may omit environments
from earlier instances.
Result statuses use the same canonical vulnerability status values as the statuses filter.
Examples:
- High-priority open: severities="CRITICAL,HIGH", statuses="Reported,Confirmed"
- Production critical with recent activity: environments="PRODUCTION",
  severities="CRITICAL", lastSeenAfter="2025-01-01"
- Remediation workflow tags: vulnTags="SmartFix Remediated", statuses="Remediated"

severities.description: Comma-separated severities: CRITICAL,HIGH,MEDIUM,LOW,NOTE. Default: all severities

statuses.description: Comma-separated vulnerability statuses: Reported,Suspicious,Confirmed,NotAProblem,Remediated,Fixed,AutoRemediated. Default: Reported,Suspicious,Confirmed (actionable only). AutoRemediated means the Agent verified a fix at runtime; Contrast did not fix it.

vulnTypes.description: Comma-separated vulnerability types (e.g., sql-injection,reflected-xss). Use list_vulnerability_types tool for complete list. Default: all types

environments.description: Comma-separated environments: DEVELOPMENT,QA,PRODUCTION. Matches any historical vulnerability instance. Default: all environments

lastSeenAfter.description: Only include vulnerabilities with LAST ACTIVITY after this date (ISO format: YYYY-MM-DD or epoch timestamp). Filters on lastTimeSeen, not discovery date

lastSeenBefore.description: Only include vulnerabilities with LAST ACTIVITY before this date (ISO format: YYYY-MM-DD or epoch timestamp). Filters on lastTimeSeen, not discovery date

vulnTags.description: Comma-separated VULNERABILITY-LEVEL tags (e.g., 'SmartFix Remediated,reviewed'). Note: These are vulnerability tags, not application tags. Use to find vulnerabilities tagged during remediation workflows

name: get_incident
description: Get full detail for one incident, including runbooks. Use search_incidents to find the incidentId. For linked issues or observation evidence, use list_incident_issues or list_incident_observations.

includeSummary.description: Also fetch the narrative summary and recommended actions. Adds one downstream call. Summaries can be absent for visible incidents.

includeObservationCount.description: Also fetch the total number of linked observations without paging the observation list. Adds one downstream call.

name: search_issues
description:
Search issues across the authenticated organization with optional filters.

Use search_applications first to find an application ID from an application name, then pass applicationIds.

Unlike search_vulnerabilities and search_app_vulnerabilities, this tool searches unified security issues (the NorthStar data model), not Classic vulnerabilities.

For a count alone, call with no cursor and pageSize=1, then read totalItems.

Examples:
- Open critical issues for one app: applicationIds="app-uuid", statuses="OPEN", severities="CRITICAL"
- Production issues with incidents: deploymentTiers="PRODUCTION", hasIncident=true
- Recent library issues: startTime="2026-01-01T00:00:00Z", targets="LIBRARY"

cursor.description: Opaque continuation token returned as nextCursor by the prior response. Send the same filters and sort as the first page. Omit for the first page.

sort.description: Sort as property,DIRECTION. Valid properties: createdAt, issueId, lastObservedTime, observationCount, score, serviceName, status, title. Use score to sort by risk because severity is derived from score. Valid directions: ASC, DESC. Default: createdAt,DESC

startTime.description: Filter by start timestamp. Accepts ISO-8601 timestamp with timezone, e.g. 2025-01-15T10:30:00Z, or epoch milliseconds. Date-only values are rejected. Default: no start-time lower bound.

endTime.description: Filter by end timestamp. Accepts ISO-8601 timestamp with timezone, e.g. 2025-01-16T10:30:00Z, or epoch milliseconds. Date-only values are rejected. Default: no end-time upper bound.

applicationIds.description: Comma-separated application IDs. Default: all applications.

repositoryNames.description: Comma-separated repository names. Default: all repositories

statuses.description: Comma-separated statuses: OPEN,CLOSED. Default: all statuses

severities.description: Comma-separated severities: CRITICAL,HIGH,MEDIUM,LOW,NOTE. Default: all severities. Note: issues without a CVSS score have no severity; downstream filtering omits them whenever this filter is set. An absent severity means unscored, not low risk.

deploymentTiers.description: Comma-separated deployment tiers: DEVELOPMENT,QA,PRODUCTION. Default: all deployment tiers

classifications.description: Comma-separated observation triage classifications: UNKNOWN,TRUE_POSITIVE,FALSE_POSITIVE. Filters by triage outcome, not vulnerability type or rule category. Default: all classifications. For vulnerability-type filtering, use searchTerms.

libraries.description: Comma-separated library names. Default: all libraries

hasIncident.description: Filter by whether an issue has an incident. Default: include issues with and without incidents

searchTerms.description: Search terms. Default: no text search

dataTypes.description: Comma-separated data types: VULNERABILITY,ATTACK,BEHAVIOR. Default: all data types

targets.description: Comma-separated targets: CODE,LIBRARY. Default: all targets

sensors.description: Comma-separated sensors: CONTRAST_AGENT,CONTRAST_SMART_SCAN. Default: all sensors

techniques.description: Comma-separated techniques: RUNTIME,STATIC. Default: all techniques

name: search_app_vulnerabilities
description:
Application-scoped vulnerability search with session-based filtering.

Requires appId. Use search_applications to find application IDs by name.

Use this instead of search_vulnerabilities when you need to filter by session metadata or latest session.

Session filtering options are mutually exclusive: use either sessionMetadataFilters or useLatestSession=true, not both.

A result's environments field reflects only its latest instance and may omit environments from earlier instances.
Result statuses use the same canonical vulnerability status values as the statuses filter.
Examples:
- Latest session vulns: appId="abc123", useLatestSession=true
- Metadata filter: appId="abc123", sessionMetadataFilters='{"branch":"main"}'
- Production critical: appId="abc123", severities="CRITICAL", environments="PRODUCTION"

statuses.description: Comma-separated vulnerability statuses: Reported,Suspicious,Confirmed,NotAProblem,Remediated,Fixed,AutoRemediated. Default: Reported,Suspicious,Confirmed (actionable only). AutoRemediated means the Agent verified a fix at runtime; Contrast did not fix it.

vulnTypes.description: Comma-separated vulnerability types. Use list_vulnerability_types for complete list

environments.description: Comma-separated environments: DEVELOPMENT,QA,PRODUCTION. Matches any historical vulnerability instance

lastSeenAfter.description: Only include vulnerabilities with LAST ACTIVITY after this date (ISO: YYYY-MM-DD or epoch)

lastSeenBefore.description: Only include vulnerabilities with LAST ACTIVITY before this date (ISO: YYYY-MM-DD or epoch)

sessionMetadataFilters.description: JSON object for session metadata filters. Format: {"fieldName":"value"} or {"fieldName":["val1","val2"]}. Multiple fields use AND logic. Multiple values within a field use OR logic. Field names are case-insensitive. Values are case-sensitive and must be non-empty.

name: get_scan_project
description:
Get a Contrast Scan (SAST) project by name, including language, scan counts, last scan ID
and time, and vulnerability counts by severity.

name: list_incident_observations
description: List observation-level evidence for one incident, cursor-paginated. Use search_incidents to find the incidentId. For the total count without paging, use get_incident with includeObservationCount=true; for full detail on one observation, use get_observation.

cursor.description: Opaque continuation token returned as nextCursor by the prior response

name: get_observation
description: Get full detail for one observation. Use list_issue_observations or list_incident_observations to find observation IDs.

name: list_application_libraries
description:
List the third-party libraries in one application, with known CVEs, severity counts,
security grade, and class usage. classesUsed 0 means no classes from that library were
seen loaded, so it is likely unused and unlikely to be exploitable. Use
search_applications to find application IDs. Use list_applications_by_cve for the reverse
direction, from a CVE to affected applications.

name: get_user_info
description: Get identity details for the authenticated user and organization.

name: get_route_coverage
description:
Get route coverage for an application: which routes have been exercised by HTTP requests
and which were only discovered. Use search_applications to find application IDs. Route
coverage requires the application to hold an Assess license; unlicensed applications
return an error.

sessionMetadataName.description: Session metadata field name to filter by (e.g., 'branch'). Must be provided with sessionMetadataValue. Use get_session_metadata to discover field names.

sessionMetadataValue.description: Session metadata field value to filter by (e.g., 'main'). Must be provided with sessionMetadataName.

useLatestSession.description: If true, only return routes from the latest session. Mutually exclusive with session metadata filter.

name: get_protect_rules
description:
Get Protect (ADR) rules for an application. Per-environment mode is one of
BLOCKING (blocked in-app), BLOCKING_PERIMETER (blocked at the perimeter),
MONITORING, MONITOR_PERIMETER, or OFF. Use search_applications to find
application IDs.

name: list_incident_issues
description: List issue summaries linked to one incident. Use search_incidents to find the incidentId, and get_issue for full issue detail.

name: get_vulnerability
description: Get full vulnerability details by ID, including remediation guidance, stack traces, and vulnerable libraries. Use search_vulnerabilities or search_app_vulnerabilities to discover vulnerability IDs. httpRequest has sensitive headers removed. environments reflects the latest instance only and may omit earlier instances.

name: search_attacks
description:
Search attacks detected by Contrast ADR (Attack Detection and Response) across the
organization, with filtering by categorization, outcome status, keyword, and rule.

Examples:
- Effective exploits: quickFilter="EFFECTIVE", statusFilter="EXPLOITED"
- Manual SQL injection: quickFilter="MANUAL", rules="sql-injection"
- Blocked attacks from one source: statusFilter="BLOCKED", keyword="192.0.2.10"

quickFilter.description: Quick filter for attack categorization. Valid: ALL (no filter), ACTIVE (ongoing attacks), MANUAL (human-initiated), AUTOMATED (bot attacks), PRODUCTION (prod environment), EFFECTIVE (excludes probed attacks)

statusFilter.description: Status filter for attack outcome. Valid: EXPLOITED (successfully exploited), PROBED (detected but not exploited), BLOCKED (blocked by Protect), BLOCKED_PERIMETER (blocked at perimeter), PROBED_PERIMETER (probed at perimeter), SUSPICIOUS (suspicious attack)

keyword.description: Keyword to match against source IP, server name/hostname, application name, rule name, attack UUID, forwarded IP/path, or attack tags (substring match, OR logic across all fields)

includeBotBlockers.description: Include attacks flagged as bot blockers

sort.description: Sort as property,DIRECTION. Valid properties: sourceIP, status, startTime, endTime, type. Valid directions: ASC, DESC. Default: startTime,DESC

rules.description: Comma-separated list of rule IDs to filter by (e.g., 'sql-injection,reflected-xss'). Use get_protect_rules to discover available rule IDs for an application. This filters by exact rule match, unlike keyword which does substring search.

name: list_applications_by_cve
description:
List applications affected by one CVE, with the vulnerable library versions and
per-application class usage. classUsage 0 or absent means no classes from the vulnerable
library were seen loaded, so exploitation is unlikely; prioritize applications with
classUsage above 0. Use list_application_libraries for the reverse direction, all
libraries of one application. Use search_applications for application lastSeenAt and
search_servers for current server state.

name: list_vulnerability_types
description:
List every vulnerability type (Assess rule name) available in the organization, such as
sql-injection or reflected-xss. Returned values are the valid inputs for the vulnTypes
parameter of search_vulnerabilities and search_app_vulnerabilities.

name: list_issue_incidents
description: List the incidents linked to one issue. Use search_issues to find the issueId, and get_incident for full detail on one incident.

name: get_session_metadata
description:
Get the session metadata fields and values recorded for an application, such as branch or
build. Field names feed sessionMetadataFilters in search_app_vulnerabilities and session
filters in get_route_coverage. Use search_applications to find application IDs.

name: get_cve_impact
description: Get CVE risk, exposure, and shield protection posture across the authenticated NorthStar organization. Use search_cves to find the cveId.

cveId.description: CVE identifier in CVE-YYYY-NNNN format (4-19 sequence digits).

name: search_servers
description:
Search servers visible to the current credentials (EAC-scoped) for inventory, agent
health, and Protect coverage.

Non-null Assess/Protect state may reflect the first visible application's effective
configuration. Protect pending-restart state is not available from this endpoint; do not
infer it (assessPending is accurate).

Examples: quickFilter="ONLINE" to inspect Protect state; quickFilter="UNPROTECTED",
environments="PRODUCTION"; environments="QA", includeApplications=true.

keyword.description: Substring match over server name, hostname, path, or tag

environments.description: Comma-separated environments. Valid: DEVELOPMENT, QA, PRODUCTION

quickFilter.description: Single condition. Valid: ALL, ONLINE, OFFLINE, PROTECTED, UNPROTECTED, OUT_OF_DATE. ONLINE/OFFLINE use TeamServer's activity threshold (typically about 50 minutes). OUT_OF_DATE means older than the newest agent TeamServer can serve for that language. To combine two dimensions, filter by one and inspect item fields for the other. Default: ALL

logLevels.description: Comma-separated log levels. Valid: ERROR, WARN, INFO, DEBUG, TRACE

includeApplications.description: Include visible application identities; default false returns applicationCount only and applications is null, not an empty list.

sort.description: Sort as property,DIRECTION. Properties: name, environment, lastActivity, agentVersion. Directions: ASC, DESC. agentVersion uses backend lexical string ordering, not semantic version ordering. Default: lastActivity,DESC

name: list_cve_issues
description:
List one issue row per affected NorthStar application and library for a CVE.

Use search_cves to find the cveId. This endpoint has no server-side filters; page through every result and read the per-environment shield status, which reflects agent-reported activity. A null environment means that deployment tier was never observed for this application, not that the shield failed. Use issueId with get_issue for full issue detail or list_issue_observations for evidence.

cveId.description: CVE identifier in CVE-YYYY-NNNN format (4-19 sequence digits).

sort.description: Sort as property,DIRECTION. Valid properties: name,version,issueId,cvssScore,severity,shieldResultProd,shieldResultQa,shieldResultDev,status,applicationName. Valid directions: ASC,DESC. Shield status properties use raw activity ordinals: NO_SHIELD -10, SHIELD_OFF -5, NOT_SEEN 0, PROTECTING 5, EXPOSED 10, BLOCKED 15, EXPLOITED 20; this is not risk ordering, and DESC puts BLOCKED above EXPOSED. Default: cvssScore,DESC for this reason. An issueId tie-breaker is appended.

cursor.description: Opaque continuation token returned as nextCursor by the prior response.

name: get_issue
description: Get full detail for one issue, including rule, repository, environments, and incident linkage. Use search_issues to find the issueId.

includeSummary.description: Also fetch the issue summary. Adds one downstream call. Only issues backed by IAST vulnerability or attack events have summaries.
